questions.q: Canada is the second largest country on earth. About how big is it?
questions.e: Canada is the second largest country on earth, with about 10 million square kilometres.

questions.q: Which three oceans border Canada?
questions.a: The Pacific, the Atlantic and the Arctic
w: The Pacific, the Indian and the Atlantic
The Atlantic, the Arctic and the Southern
The Indian, the Arctic and the Pacific
questions.e: Three oceans line Canada's frontiers: the Pacific Ocean in the west, the Atlantic Ocean in the east and the Arctic Ocean to the north.

questions.q: Which ocean is on Canada's west coast?
questions.e: The Pacific Ocean is in the west, the Atlantic in the east and the Arctic to the north.

questions.q: Which country borders Canada to the south?
questions.e: Along the southern edge of Canada lies the Canada-United States boundary.

questions.q: What are the five regions of Canada?
questions.a: The Atlantic Provinces, Central Canada, the Prairie Provinces, the West Coast and the Northern Territories
w: The North, the South, the East, the West and the Centre
Ontario, Quebec, the Maritimes, the Prairies and the Rockies
The Arctic, the Pacific, the Atlantic, the Great Lakes and the Prairies
questions.e: Canada has five regions: the Atlantic Provinces, Central Canada, the Prairie Provinces, the West Coast and the Northern Territories.

questions.q: How many provinces and territories does Canada have?
questions.e: Canada has ten provinces and three territories.

questions.q: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.e: The national capital is Ottawa, on the Ottawa River.

questions.q: Who chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857?
questions.e: Ottawa was chosen as the capital by Queen Victoria in 1857.

questions.q: About how many people live in Canada today?
questions.e: Canada's population is now about 41 million. Older copies of Discover Canada say about 34 million.

questions.q: Most Canadians live in cities.
questions.e: Most of Canada's population lives in cities, many of them close to the border with the United States.

questions.q: Which provinces are the Atlantic Provinces?
questions.a: Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick
w: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick
Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Quebec
questions.e: The Atlantic Provinces are Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick.

questions.q: Which province is the most easterly point in North America and has its own time zone?
questions.e: Newfoundland and Labrador is the most easterly point in North America and has its own time zone.

questions.q: Which province is known as the oldest colony of the British Empire?
questions.e: Newfoundland and Labrador is the oldest colony of the British Empire and a strategic prize in Canada's early history.

questions.q: Newfoundland and Labrador is known for its fisheries, coastal fishing villages and offshore oil.
questions.e: Newfoundland and Labrador is known for its fisheries, coastal fishing villages and distinct culture. Offshore oil and gas extraction contribute to the economy.

questions.q: Which is the smallest province in Canada?
questions.e: Prince Edward Island (P.E.I.) is the smallest province, known for its beaches, red soil and agriculture, especially potatoes.

questions.q: Prince Edward Island is known for growing which crop?
questions.e: P.E.I. is known for its beaches, red soil and agriculture, especially potatoes.

questions.q: Which bridge links Prince Edward Island to mainland New Brunswick?
questions.e: P.E.I. is connected to mainland Canada by the Confederation Bridge, one of the longest continuous multi-span bridges in the world.

questions.q: Which city is called the birthplace of Confederation?
questions.e: P.E.I. is known as the birthplace of Confederation. The Charlottetown Conference of 1864 began the talks that led to Confederation.

questions.q: Which is the most populous Atlantic province?
questions.e: Nova Scotia is the most populous Atlantic province, with a rich history as the gateway to Canada.

questions.q: Where are the highest tides in the world?
questions.e: Nova Scotia is known for the highest tides in the world in the Bay of Fundy.

questions.q: What was Pier 21 in Halifax?
questions.a: The gateway for more than one million immigrants to Canada from 1928 to 1971
w: The site of the first Parliament
A navy base for the War of 1812
questions.e: Pier 21 in Halifax was the gateway to Canada for more than one million immigrants from 1928 to 1971. It is now a national museum.

questions.q: Halifax has played an important role in Atlantic trade and defence and is home to Canada's largest naval base.
questions.e: The capital, Halifax, has played an important role in Atlantic trade and defence and is home to Canada's largest naval base.

questions.q: Which is the only officially bilingual province?
questions.e: New Brunswick is the only officially bilingual province. About one-third of the population lives and works in French.

questions.q: Which mountain range is in New Brunswick?
questions.e: New Brunswick is situated in the Appalachian Range. It was founded by the Loyalists and still has the only officially bilingual province.

questions.q: Nova Scotia has a strong Celtic and Gaelic heritage.
questions.e: Nova Scotia is known for its Celtic heritage, with Gaelic culture and music still celebrated, especially on Cape Breton Island.

questions.q: Which two provinces make up Central Canada?
questions.e: Central Canada is made up of Quebec and Ontario.

questions.q: Where do more than half of Canadians live?
questions.a: In cities and towns near the Great Lakes and the St. Lawrence River in Ontario and Quebec
questions.e: More than half the people in Canada live in cities and towns near the Great Lakes and the St. Lawrence River in southern Quebec and Ontario.

questions.q: What do most people in Quebec speak as their first language?
questions.e: Quebec has nearly 8 million people, most living along or near the St. Lawrence River. More than three-quarters speak French as their first language.

questions.q: Quebec is a leader in producing which kind of electricity?
questions.e: Quebec's resources, including vast forests, minerals and water, have made it a leader in producing cheap, clean hydroelectricity.

questions.q: Which is Canada's second largest city and the second largest mainly French-speaking city in the world?
questions.e: Montreal, Canada's second largest city, is the second largest mainly French-speaking city in the world, after Paris.

questions.q: Which province has the most people?
questions.e: More than one-third of Canadians live in Ontario, home to more people than any other province.

questions.q: What is Canada's largest city and main financial centre?
questions.e: Toronto is the largest city in Canada and the country's main financial centre.

questions.q: Which are the five Great Lakes?
questions.a: Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie and Superior
w: Huron, Ontario, Winnipeg, Erie and Superior
Superior, Michigan, Champlain, Ontario and Erie
Great Bear, Great Slave, Huron, Erie and Ontario
questions.e: The five Great Lakes, located between Ontario and the United States, are Lake Huron, Lake Ontario, Lake Michigan, Lake Erie and Lake Superior.

questions.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world (by area)?
questions.e: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

questions.q: The Niagara region of Ontario is known for its vineyards and fruit farms.
questions.e: Ontario's Niagara region is known for its vineyards, wines and fruit crops.

questions.q: Which provinces are the Prairie Provinces?
w: Saskatchewan, Alberta and the Northwest Territories
questions.e: Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta are the Prairie Provinces, rich in energy resources and some of the most fertile farmland in the world.

questions.q: What is Manitoba's economy based on?
questions.e: Manitoba's economy is based on agriculture, mining and hydroelectric power generation.

questions.q: Which community in Winnipeg is the largest francophone community in Western Canada?
questions.e: Winnipeg's Saint-Boniface is the largest francophone community in Western Canada.

questions.q: Manitoba is an important centre of Ukrainian culture.
questions.e: Manitoba is an important centre of Ukrainian culture and has the largest Aboriginal population of any province.

questions.q: Which province was once known as the 'breadbasket of the world' and the 'wheat province'?
questions.e: Saskatchewan, once known as the 'breadbasket of the world' and the 'wheat province', has 40% of the arable land in Canada and is the country's largest producer of grains and oilseeds.

questions.q: Saskatchewan has the world's largest deposits of which minerals?
questions.e: Saskatchewan has the world's richest deposits of uranium and potash, used in fertilizer.

questions.q: In which city is the training academy of the RCMP?
questions.e: Regina, the capital of Saskatchewan, is home to the training academy of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

questions.q: Which is the most populous Prairie province?
questions.e: Alberta is the most populous Prairie province.

questions.q: After whom is the province of Alberta named?
questions.a: Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, fourth daughter of Queen Victoria
w: The first Premier of the province
questions.e: The province, and the famous Lake Louise in the Rocky Mountains, were both named after Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, the fourth daughter of Queen Victoria.

questions.q: Which province is the largest producer of oil and gas?
questions.e: Alberta is the largest producer of oil and gas, and the oil sands in the north are being developed as a major energy source.

questions.q: Which is Canada's oldest national park, established in 1885?
questions.e: Alberta has five national parks, including Banff National Park, established in 1885.

questions.q: Alberta is known for its cattle ranches and beef.
questions.e: Alberta is renowned for agriculture, especially for the vast cattle ranches that make Canada one of the world's major beef producers.

questions.q: The rugged Badlands of Alberta hold some of the world's richest deposits of dinosaur fossils.
questions.e: The rugged Badlands house some of the richest deposits of prehistoric fossils and dinosaur finds in the world.

questions.q: Which province is on Canada's west coast?
questions.e: British Columbia, on the Pacific coast, is Canada's westernmost province.

questions.q: Which is Canada's largest and busiest port, and its gateway to the Asia-Pacific?
questions.e: The Port of Vancouver is our gateway to the Asia-Pacific. It is Canada's largest and busiest port.

questions.q: What is the capital of British Columbia?
questions.e: Victoria, the capital, is a tourist centre and headquarters of the navy's Pacific fleet.

questions.q: Which of these is a major industry in British Columbia?
questions.e: About half of all the goods produced in B.C. are forestry products. B.C. is also known for mining, fishing, fruit orchards and wine in the Okanagan Valley.

questions.q: British Columbia has a strong Asian heritage, and Chinese and Punjabi are widely spoken in its cities.
questions.e: Because of its trade and immigration links with Asia, B.C. has a strong Asian heritage. Chinese and Punjabi are the most spoken languages in its cities after English.

questions.q: Which are Canada's three territories?
questions.a: Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut
w: The Northwest Territories, Alaska and Nunavut
Yukon, Manitoba and the Northwest Territories
questions.e: The Northwest Territories, Nunavut and Yukon make up one-third of Canada's land mass.

questions.q: The three territories make up about how much of Canada's land mass?
questions.e: The three territories make up one-third of Canada's land mass but have a small population of a little over 100,000 people.

questions.q: Why is the North called the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'?
questions.a: In summer, daylight can last up to 24 hours
w: The sun never rises in summer
The sun only shines at midnight in winter
questions.e: The North is often called the 'Land of the Midnight Sun' because in summer, daylight can last up to 24 hours. In winter, the sun disappears and darkness sets in for three months.

questions.q: What brought thousands of miners to Yukon in the 1890s?
questions.e: Thousands of miners came to Yukon during the Gold Rush of the 1890s, as celebrated in the poetry of Robert W. Service.

questions.q: What is the capital of Yukon?
questions.e: Whitehorse is the capital of Yukon.

questions.q: The coldest temperature ever recorded in Canada, −63°C, was in Yukon.
questions.e: Yukon holds the record for the coldest temperature ever recorded in Canada, −63°C.

questions.q: What is the capital of the Northwest Territories, known as the 'diamond capital of North America'?
questions.e: Yellowknife, the capital of the Northwest Territories, is called the 'diamond capital of North America'.

questions.q: Which river in the Northwest Territories is one of the longest river systems in North America?
questions.e: The Mackenzie River, 4,200 km long, is the second-longest river system in North America after the Mississippi.

questions.q: More than half the people of the Northwest Territories are Aboriginal.
questions.e: More than half the population of the Northwest Territories is Aboriginal (Dene, Inuit and Métis).

questions.q: What does 'Nunavut' mean in Inuktitut?
questions.e: Nunavut, meaning 'our land' in Inuktitut, was established in 1999 from the eastern part of the Northwest Territories.

questions.q: In which year was Nunavut created?
questions.e: Nunavut was established in 1999 from the eastern part of the Northwest Territories.

questions.q: What is the capital of Nunavut?
questions.e: The capital of Nunavut is Iqaluit, formerly Frobisher Bay, named after the English explorer Martin Frobisher.

questions.q: About what share of the population of Nunavut is Inuit?
questions.e: About 85% of the population of Nunavut is Inuit. The Legislative Assembly of 19 members chooses a premier and ministers by consensus.

questions.q: Who are the Canadian Rangers?
questions.a: Part of the Canadian Forces Reserves who patrol and protect the remote North
questions.e: The Canadian Rangers, part of the Canadian Forces Reserves, play a key role in Canada's Arctic sovereignty by patrolling the remote North.

questions.q: What is the capital of Ontario?
questions.e: Toronto is the capital of Ontario. Ottawa, also in Ontario, is the capital of Canada.

questions.q: What is the capital of Quebec?
questions.e: Quebec City is the capital of the province of Quebec.

questions.q: What is the capital of Nova Scotia?
questions.e: Halifax is the capital of Nova Scotia.

questions.q: What is the capital of New Brunswick?
questions.e: Fredericton is the capital of New Brunswick.

questions.q: What is the capital of Prince Edward Island?
questions.e: Charlottetown is the capital of Prince Edward Island.

questions.q: What is the capital of Newfoundland and Labrador?
questions.e: St. John's is the capital of Newfoundland and Labrador. Do not confuse it with Saint John, the largest city in New Brunswick.

questions.q: What is the capital of Manitoba?
questions.e: Winnipeg is the capital of Manitoba.

questions.q: What is the capital of Saskatchewan?
questions.e: Regina is the capital of Saskatchewan.

questions.q: What is the capital of Alberta?
questions.e: Edmonton is the capital of Alberta.

questions.q: Toronto is the capital of Canada.
questions.e: Ottawa is the capital of Canada. Toronto is the capital of Ontario.

questions.q: Quebec is the only officially bilingual province.
questions.e: New Brunswick is the only officially bilingual province.

questions.q: British Columbia is one of the Prairie Provinces.
questions.e: The Prairie Provinces are Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta. British Columbia is on the West Coast.

questions.q: Nunavut was created in 1867.
questions.e: Nunavut was created in 1999 from the eastern part of the Northwest Territories.

questions.q: Whitehorse is the capital of Nunavut.
questions.e: Iqaluit is the capital of Nunavut. Whitehorse is the capital of Yukon.
